newsitem.title: USA: Gumbel, formerly of NBC Today Show, signs with CBS.
newsitem.headline: Gumbel, formerly of NBC Today Show, signs with CBS.

text.p: Bryant Gumbel, who presided over NBC's "Today" show for a record 15 years, winning a huge following, joined opposition CBS Thursday, signing a five-year deal that the network viewed as a major step in rebuilding its ratings-battered news division.

Gumbel, who gave up hosting the Today show in January, told a a news conference he would have his own weekly primetime news magazine show starting in September and form his own company to produce specials for CBS and develop programmes for other markets.
"I am very excited ... This is a very happy day for me," he said, adding that it was a close call whether to sign with CBS, owned by Westinghouse Electric Corp., or General Electric Co.'s NBC.

"I have nothing bad to say about any of them," he said of his former employer, adding that he planned to continue playing golf with General Electric Chairman Jack Welsh. He declined to talk about terms of the CBS deal but broadcasting sources said he will be paid between $5 million and $7 million a year, easily doubling what he earned at NBC.

Andrew Heyward, head of CBS news, said Gumbel's primetime show was still being developed, but he and Gumbel both said it would be partially broadcast live and would stress Gumbel's interviewing skills.

"Bryant is a key to our expanding to new areas," Heyward said, adding that at no time in their talks was there any discussion of Gumbel possibly replacing Dan Rather as anchor of the CBS Evening News, which is third in the ratings for network news programmes.
Gumbel stressed that he had no interest in being an evening news anchorman and added that in all his years at NBC he never once hosted an evening programme, "not even on weekends."
After the news conference, Westinghouse Chairman Michael Jordan said he wholeheartedly approved of the deal because "we are not going to win in this business by doing what we have been doing."
